clue.text: Force man to study in the law firm

indicators.note: the word for study sits within the phrase built from the law and firm, so in marks a container

parts.note: the police are informally called the law
stable means firm or steady
to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: Someone is forced to go and study inside a legal practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force man' reads like a command to compel a man; it is the definition, a man in the police force.
explanation.definitionFit: A uniformed officer of the lowest rank is a man of the police force, so a force man.

clue.text: Some silver providing class in epic fence off

indicators.note: the words for providing and class go inside the rearranged letters, so in marks a container
off in the sense of gone bad or wrong signals that the letters of epic fence are jumbled

parts.note: providing means if, as a condition
a type is a class or kind

explanation.surface: Something silvery providing class inside an epic fence that has come off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals the anagram; the inserted words go in just after its first letter. The fifty pence piece is a British coin of silver-coloured cupronickel.
explanation.definitionFit: British coins of silver colour are loosely called silver, and this coin is one example of such loose change.

clue.text: Rioting from troops resistant to the force of powerful elements

definitions.text: resistant to the force of powerful elements

indicators.note: rioting means running wild, so the letters of from troops are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Rioting by soldiers, from which something is protected against the force of the elements.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made to withstand gales and heavy weather resists the strength of the natural elements.

clue.text: Gauge measurement for Berkshire town

definitions.meaning: the figure shown on a meter or dial is what it reads off
a large town in the county of Berkshire, west of London

explanation.surface: A railway gauge being measured near a town in Berkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A dial's figure is its reading, and Reading is a large town in Berkshire, a county west of London.

clue.text: Wine tipped up into fruit salad

indicators.note: in a down clue tipped up means turned upwards, so the letters are read from bottom to top
the wine is found going into the words fruit salad, so into marks a hidden run of letters

explanation.surface: Wine has been poured upwards into a bowl of fruit salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' finds ITSA in fruIT SAlad, and 'tipped up' turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian sparkling white from Piedmont, named after the town where it is made.

clue.text: Musicians welcoming five hundred dancing emus gatecrashing concert, as not much on when swimming in Australia?

definitions.text: not much on when swimming in Australia

indicators.note: the musicians take in the rest of the pieces, as hosts welcoming guests, so it marks a container

parts.note: buglers are musicians who play the bugle
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

indicators.note: the jumbled birds force their way into the concert, so gatecrashing marks insertion

parts.note: a gig is a concert

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so the letters of emus are rearranged

explanation.surface: Musicians hosting dancing emus at a gig, which makes an image of Australian beachwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' scrambles the birds, 'gatecrashing' puts them inside the concert, and 'welcoming' has the musicians hold everything after their second letter. Budgie smugglers is Australian slang for tight men's swimming briefs.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang for brief, tight men's swimming trunks, which cover very little of the swimmer.

clue.text: See 8
Around the third of January, today it's cold for our dance marquee — so play begins

parts.note: now means at the present time, today
when it is cold, it is the winter season
of can stand for for, as in love of or love for

indicators.note: the dance and marquee words go around a single letter, so around marks a container

parts.note: a disco is a dance
a marquee is a large tent

indicators.note: the third of signals taking the third letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Early January, and today it is too cold for our dance tent, so a show starts instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' is placed first but wraps the dance and marquee words at the end. The answer is the opening line of Shakespeare's Richard III, spoken by Richard himself.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous first line of Richard III is how that Shakespeare drama starts.

clue.text: Ram and monkey finally getting close

parts.note: to ram something in is to stuff it

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of the word monkey

explanation.surface: A ram and a monkey eventually draw near to each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ram' and 'close' look like nouns and an adjective of distance; they are a verb and the airless sense of close.
explanation.definitionFit: Close weather or air is stale, warm and airless, which is the same as stuffy.

clue.text: See 8
Beginning to disprove negative principle, disease on the decline

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of the word disprove

parts.note: yin is the passive, negative principle of Chinese philosophy
gout is a disease of the joints

explanation.surface: Starting to disprove a negative theory that a disease is in retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in decline is fading away towards extinction, gradually ceasing to exist.

clue.text: Bound to find drink laced with drug

indicators.note: a drink laced with something has it added inside, so this marks a container

parts.note: to lap is to drink, as a cat does
E is short for ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: Someone is sure to find a spiked drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' reads as certain to; it is a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound is a jump, so the two words are synonyms as nouns or verbs.

clue.text: Informal correspondents retain a day to send letters

parts.note: to pen animals is to keep them in an enclosure, to retain them
Fri is short for Friday

indicators.note: the letters of send are taken and shuffled about, so letters marks the rearrangement here

explanation.surface: Correspondents keep one day aside for posting letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' rearranges SEND to ENDS. It looks like part of the picture of posting mail.
explanation.definitionFit: People who write regularly to each other as friends, often strangers abroad, correspond informally by post.

clue.text: Partition in church, where orders once carried out

indicators.note: carried out suggests doing, but here the letters of orders once are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A church partition where orders were once followed.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved screen dividing nave from chancel, topped by a crucifix, the rood.

clue.text: Unhappy to concede a stroke as a player

parts.note: down means low in spirits, unhappy
to bow to someone is to yield or concede

explanation.surface: A sad sportsman conceding a stroke in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stroke' and 'player' suggest golf; the player is a string musician.
explanation.definitionFit: A violinist or cellist draws the bow downwards across the strings in this stroke.

clue.text: Spar with Cameron amid cheers, perhaps

indicators.note: the leader's title is placed in the middle of the drinking word, so amid marks insertion

parts.note: cheers is an example of a toast
David Cameron was the UK Prime Minister, PM, when this was set

explanation.surface: Sparring with David Cameron while people raise glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spar' reads as a verb, to box; it is a ship's pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A topmast is a pole of a ship's rigging, the section above the lower mast, so a kind of spar.

clue.text: Hole in small chamber where bread absorbs much water

indicators.note: one word takes in the other, as bread soaks up liquid, so absorbs marks a container

parts.note: bread and loot are both slang for money
a sea is a great deal of water

explanation.surface: A hole in a small room where bread soaks up a lot of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' is slang for money, here LOOT. The small chamber is the toilet, often called the smallest room.
explanation.definitionFit: The ring with a hole that one sits on in the smallest room of the house, the toilet.

clue.text: Entering Fido's ground, sign has got significance primarily in this part of London?

indicators.note: the star sign goes into the jumbled letters, so entering marks insertion
ground means crushed or milled, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the dog's name with the possessive s

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letters of got and significance

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A sign enters a dog's patch and gains meaning in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' shuffles the dog's name with the two first letters into ISFDOGS, and the star sign enters after its second letter. The Isle of Dogs is a district of East London, home to Canary Wharf.
explanation.definitionFit: A peninsula in a loop of the Thames in East London, which suits Fido's ground.

clue.text: Please continue to be a thug

definitions.meaning: an urging to carry on talking or acting

explanation.surface: Urging someone to carry on being a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase urges a speaker on, and run together it is the word for a hired heavy.

clue.text: Transport around a cold, getting sick — that's a bug

indicators.note: the vehicle goes around the other pieces, so around marks a container

parts.note: a bus is public transport
C is short for cold, as on a tap
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Riding the bus with a cold and feeling sick, from a germ.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod-shaped bacterium is a germ, which is loosely called a bug.

clue.text: Say something to spring vegetable

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, giving one that sounds the same

parts.note: a boat or pipe can spring a leak

explanation.surface: Talking about a vegetable bursting into the springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' wants to be the season; it is the verb in springing a leak.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion-family plant with a long white stalk, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Tell supporter at the back to cheer

indicators.note: at the back picks the final letter of the word supporter

parts.note: to elate someone is to cheer them

explanation.surface: Telling a supporter at the rear of the stand to cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to tell or narrate it.

clue.text: See short man in woman's hat

indicators.note: short means cut, so the word for see loses its final letter

parts.note: to clock something is slang for to see or notice it
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: Seeing a small man inside a lady's hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short man' looks like one phrase; 'short' trims CLOCK, and 'man' is HE.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting bell-shaped hat worn by women, popular in the 1920s.

clue.text: Jack, queen, king and ace not extremely unusual

parts.note: a jack tar is a sailor, AB for able seaman
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
R stands for rex, king
A is the card abbreviation for ace

indicators.note: extremely picks the outer letters of the word not

explanation.surface: Four playing cards in a row, and not entirely unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack, queen, king and ace' look like playing cards; only ace is.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberrant behaviour departs from the norm, which makes it unusual or abnormal.
